youtube.title: Toys R Us: The $6.6 Billion Deal Behind 735 Closed Stores
youtube.description:
In 2005 three investors agreed to buy Toys R Us for $6.6 billion, mostly with borrowed money, and the debt landed on the company. Thirteen years later every US store was closing. Was it the buyout, or something that started earlier?

This documentary follows the decision from the board's 2004 review to the 2005 sale, the roughly $400 million yearly interest bill, the 2017 bankruptcy and the 2018 liquidation. It also covers the 2000 Amazon contract that cost Toys R Us years online, and where the money, the workers and the name ended up.

{CHAPTERS}

youtube.comment: Debt, Amazon or Walmart: which one really ended Toys R Us? 👇

sources.claim: The last Toys R Us stores in the US closed on June 29, 2018
sources.source: The New York Times and CNBC reporting, June 29, 2018

sources.claim: About 33,000 US jobs were lost in the liquidation
sources.source: The New York Times, March 15, 2018

sources.claim: Roughly 735 US stores were to be closed or sold
sources.source: The New York Times and Reuters, March 15, 2018

sources.claim: On March 17, 2005 KKR, Bain Capital and Vornado agreed to buy Toys R Us for $26.75 a share, about $6.6 billion
sources.source: Toys R Us press release, March 17, 2005; The New York Times, March 18, 2005

sources.claim: The buyers put in about $1.3 billion of equity; about $5.3 billion was borrowed
sources.source: The New York Times and Bloomberg reporting on the bankruptcy, September 2017

sources.claim: The debt was carried by Toys R Us itself
sources.source: Toys R Us Form 10-K, fiscal 2005 (filed 2006)

sources.claim: The company began in 1948 as a baby-furniture store in Washington, D.C., opened by a young army veteran
sources.source: The New York Times obituary of the founder, March 22, 2018

sources.claim: The founder saw that families bought one crib but kept buying toys
sources.source: The New York Times obituary of the founder, March 22, 2018

sources.claim: The Toys R Us name was adopted in 1957
sources.source: The New York Times obituary of the founder, March 22, 2018

sources.claim: Net sales of $11.1 billion in fiscal 2004 from about 1,500 stores worldwide
sources.source: Toys R Us Form 10-K, fiscal 2004 (filed April 2005)

sources.claim: Walmart passed Toys R Us as America's biggest toy seller by 1998
sources.source: NPD Group data reported by The New York Times, 1999

sources.claim: FAO filed for bankruptcy twice in 2003 and KB Toys filed in January 2004
sources.source: The New York Times, January 2004

sources.claim: On August 10, 2000 Toys R Us signed a 10-year exclusive deal making Amazon its online toy store, paying $50 million a year plus a share of sales
sources.source: The New York Times, August 2000; Toys R Us v. Amazon, N.J. Superior Court, 2006

sources.claim: Toys R Us sued Amazon in 2004 over other sellers listing toys
sources.source: Toys R Us v. Amazon, N.J. Superior Court complaint, May 2004

sources.claim: On March 2, 2006 the court ruled Toys R Us could end the Amazon deal
sources.source: Toys R Us v. Amazon, N.J. Superior Court ruling, March 2, 2006

sources.claim: On August 11, 2004 the board said it would review options, including selling the toy business and keeping Babies R Us
sources.source: Toys R Us press release and The New York Times, August 11-12, 2004

sources.claim: Bidders sought the whole company including its real estate; Vornado is a property trust
sources.source: The New York Times, March 18, 2005

sources.claim: Shareholders approved the sale in June 2005; it closed on July 21, 2005
sources.source: Toys R Us Form 8-K filings, June and July 2005

sources.claim: In a sale of control, directors must seek the best value reasonably available to shareholders
sources.source: Revlon v. MacAndrews & Forbes, Delaware Supreme Court, 1986

sources.claim: 'Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our financial health'
sources.source: Toys R Us Form 10-K risk factors, fiscal 2005 onward

sources.claim: The company paid its owners advisory and transaction fees under a disclosed advisory agreement
sources.source: Toys R Us Form 10-K, related-party transactions, fiscal 2005 onward

sources.claim: Interest cost roughly $400 million a year
sources.source: Toys R Us first-day bankruptcy declaration, September 2017; CNBC, September 19, 2017

sources.claim: On May 28, 2010 Toys R Us filed to go public again to raise up to $800 million; the filing was withdrawn in 2013
sources.source: Toys R Us Form S-1, May 28, 2010; Reuters, 2013
Toys R Us Form 10-K filings, fiscal 2004-2016

sources.claim: Amazon, Walmart and Target competed on toy prices
sources.source: The New York Times, September 19, 2017

sources.claim: About $400 million of debt was due in 2018

sources.source: Toys R Us first-day bankruptcy declaration, September 2017; CNBC, September 2017
